**Generative artificial intelligence** (**Generative AI**, **GenAI**,**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-1)** or **GAI**) is a subfield of [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") that uses [generative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") to produce text, images, videos, or other forms of data.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-4) These models [learn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") the underlying patterns and structures of their [training data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_data "Training data") and use them to produce new data[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:02-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-6) based on the input, which often comes in the form of natural language [prompts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_(natural_language) "Prompt (natural language)").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes2-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-bloomberg2-8)

Generative AI tools have become more common since the [AI boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom") in the 2020s. This boom was made possible by improvements in [transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)")-based [deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning")[neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_networks "Neural networks"), particularly [large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model") (LLMs). Major tools include [chatbots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbots "Chatbots") such as [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"), [Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot "Microsoft Copilot"), [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(chatbot) "Gemini (chatbot)"), [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(language_model) "Claude (language model)"), [Grok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grok_(chatbot) "Grok (chatbot)"), and [DeepSeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot) "DeepSeek (chatbot)"); [text-to-image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image "Text-to-image") models such as [Stable Diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion "Stable Diffusion"), [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney"), and [DALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DALL-E "DALL-E"); and [text-to-video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-video "Text-to-video") models such as [Veo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veo_(text-to-video_model) "Veo (text-to-video model)") and [Sora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sora_(text-to-video_model) "Sora (text-to-video model)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes-gpt4-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:4-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-auto-13) Technology companies developing generative AI include [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"), [xAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XAI_(company) "XAI (company)"), [Anthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic "Anthropic"), [Meta AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_AI "Meta AI"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), [DeepSeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek "DeepSeek"), and [Baidu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baidu "Baidu").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes2-7)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-economist1-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-15)

Generative AI is used across many industries, including software development,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-16) healthcare,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-17) finance,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-18) entertainment,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-19) customer service,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-20) sales and marketing,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-economist2-21) art, writing,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-22) fashion,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-mckinsey-23) and product design.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-24) The production of generative AI systems requires large scale data centers using specialized chips which require a lot of electricity for processing and water for cooling.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-25)

Generative AI has raised many ethical questions and governance challenges as it can be used for [cybercrime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercrime "Cybercrime"), or to deceive or manipulate people through [fake news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_news "Fake news") or [deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfake "Deepfake").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-27) Even if used ethically, it may lead to [mass replacement of human jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_unemployment "Technological unemployment").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-28) The tools themselves have been criticized as violating intellectual property laws, since they are trained on copyrighted works.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-29) The material and energy intensity of the AI systems has raised concerns about the [environmental impact of AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impact_of_AI "Environmental impact of AI"), especially in light of the challenges created by the [energy transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_transition "Energy transition").

History
-------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_artificial_intelligence "History of artificial intelligence")

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

The first example of an algorithmically generated media is likely the [Markov chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_chain "Markov chain"). Markov chains have long been used to model natural languages since their development by Russian mathematician [Andrey Markov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrey_Markov "Andrey Markov") in the early 20th century. Markov published his first paper on the topic in 1906,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-GrinsteadSnell1997page4643-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Bremaud2013pageIX3-31) and analyzed the pattern of vowels and consonants in the novel _[Eugeny Onegin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugeny\_Onegin "Eugeny Onegin")_ using Markov chains. Once a Markov chain is trained on a [text corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus"), it can then be used as a probabilistic text generator.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-33)

Computers were needed to go beyond Markov chains. By the early 1970s, [Harold Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Cohen_(artist) "Harold Cohen (artist)") was creating and exhibiting generative AI works created by [AARON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AARON "AARON"), the computer program Cohen created to generate paintings.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-34)

The terms generative [AI planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_planning "AI planning") or generative planning were used in the 1980s and 1990s to refer to [AI planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_planning "AI planning") systems, especially [computer-aided process planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-aided_process_planning "Computer-aided process planning"), used to generate sequences of actions to reach a specified goal.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-alting-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-36) Generative AI planning systems used [symbolic AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_AI "Symbolic AI") methods such as [state space search](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search "State space search") and [constraint satisfaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constraint_satisfaction "Constraint satisfaction") and were a "relatively mature" technology by the early 1990s. They were used to generate crisis action plans for military use,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-37) process plans for manufacturing[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-alting-35) and decision plans such as in prototype autonomous spacecraft.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-38)

### Generative neural networks (2014–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Generative neural networks (2014–2019)")]

See also: [Machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning")

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png/250px-Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png)

Above: An [image classifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_classifier "Image classifier"), an example of a neural network trained with a [discriminative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") objective. Below: A [text-to-image model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image_model "Text-to-image model"), an example of a network trained with a [generative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") objective.

Since its inception, the field of [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") has used both [discriminative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") and [generative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") to model and predict data. Beginning in the late 2000s, the emergence of [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") drove progress, and research in [image classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_classification "Image classification"), [speech recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition "Speech recognition"), [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing") and other tasks. [Neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network "Neural network") in this era were typically trained as [discriminative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") models due to the difficulty of generative modeling.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-39)

In 2014, advancements such as the [variational autoencoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_autoencoder "Variational autoencoder") and [generative adversarial network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_adversarial_network "Generative adversarial network") produced the first practical deep neural networks capable of learning generative models, as opposed to discriminative ones, for complex data such as images. These deep generative models were the first to output not only class labels for images but also entire images.

In 2017, the [Transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)") network enabled advancements in generative models compared to older [long short-term memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory "Long short-term memory") (LSTM) models,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-40) leading to the first [generative pre-trained transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer "Generative pre-trained transformer") (GPT), known as [GPT-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-1 "GPT-1"), in 2018.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-41) This was followed in 2019 by [GPT-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-2 "GPT-2"), which demonstrated the ability to generalize unsupervised to many different tasks as a [Foundation model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_model "Foundation model").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-42)

The new generative models introduced during this period allowed for large neural networks to be trained using [unsupervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsupervised_learning "Unsupervised learning") or [semi-supervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-supervised_learning "Semi-supervised learning"), rather than the [supervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning "Supervised learning") typical of discriminative models. Unsupervised learning removed the need for humans to [manually label data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labeled_data "Labeled data"), allowing for larger networks to be trained.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-43)

### Generative AI boom (2020–)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Generative AI boom (2020–)")]

Main article: [AI boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom")

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png/250px-Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png)

AI generated images have become much more advanced.

In March 2020, the release of [15.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai"), a free [web application](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application "Web application") created by an anonymous [MIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT "MIT") researcher that could generate convincing character voices using minimal training data, marked one of the earliest popular use cases of generative AI.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-44) The platform is credited as the first mainstream service to popularize AI voice cloning ([audio deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_deepfakes "Audio deepfakes")) in [memes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") and [content creation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_creation "Content creation"), influencing subsequent developments in [voice AI technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning_speech_synthesis "Deep learning speech synthesis").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-46)

In 2021, the emergence of [DALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DALL-E "DALL-E"), a [transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)")-based pixel generative model, marked an advance in AI-generated imagery.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-47) This was followed by the releases of [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney") and [Stable Diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion "Stable Diffusion") in 2022, which further democratized access to high-quality [artificial intelligence art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_art "Artificial intelligence art") creation from [natural language prompts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_engineering "Prompt engineering").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-48) These systems demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in generating photorealistic images, artwork, and designs based on text descriptions, leading to widespread adoption among artists, designers, and the general public.

In late 2022, the public release of [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT") revolutionized the accessibility and [application of generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence "Applications of artificial intelligence") for general-purpose text-based tasks.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-49) The system's ability to [engage in natural conversations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot"), [generate creative content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_art "AI art"), assist with coding, and perform various analytical tasks captured global attention and sparked widespread discussion about AI's potential impact on [work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_in_industry "AI in industry"), [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_in_education "AI in education"), and [creativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_art "AI art").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-51)

In March 2023, [GPT-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4 "GPT-4")'s release represented another jump in generative AI capabilities. A team from [Microsoft Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Research "Microsoft Research") controversially argued that it "could reasonably be viewed as an early (yet still incomplete) version of an [artificial general intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence") (AGI) system."[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Bubeck-2023-52) However, this assessment was contested by other scholars who maintained that generative AI remained "still far from reaching the benchmark of 'general human intelligence'" as of 2023.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Schlagwein-2023-53) Later in 2023, [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") released [ImageBind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImageBind "ImageBind"), an AI model combining multiple [modalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modality_(human%E2%80%93computer_interaction) "Modality (human–computer interaction)") including text, images, video, thermal data, 3D data, audio, and motion, paving the way for more immersive generative AI applications.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-54)

In December 2023, [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") unveiled [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(language_model) "Gemini (language model)"), a multimodal AI model available in four versions: Ultra, Pro, Flash, and Nano.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-AnnounceWSJ-55) The company integrated Gemini Pro into its [Bard chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bard_chatbot "Bard chatbot") and announced plans for "Bard Advanced" powered by the larger Gemini Ultra model.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-56) In February 2024, Google unified Bard and Duet AI under the Gemini brand, launching a mobile app on [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and integrating the service into the Google app on [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-57)

In March 2024, [Anthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic "Anthropic") released the [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(AI) "Claude (AI)") 3 family of large language models, including Claude 3 Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-58) The models demonstrated significant improvements in capabilities across various benchmarks, with Claude 3 Opus notably outperforming leading models from OpenAI and Google.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-59) In June 2024, Anthropic released Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which demonstrated improved performance compared to the larger Claude 3 Opus, particularly in areas such as coding, multistep workflows, and image analysis.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-60)

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg/250px-Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg)

Private investment in AI (pink) and generative AI (green).

[Asia–Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia%E2%80%93Pacific "Asia–Pacific") countries are significantly more optimistic than Western societies about generative AI and show higher adoption rates. Despite expressing concerns about privacy and the pace of change, in a 2024 survey, 68% of Asia-Pacific respondents believed that AI was having a positive impact on the world, compared to 57% globally.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-61) According to a survey by [SAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAS_Institute "SAS Institute") and Coleman Parkes Research, [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in particular has emerged as a global leader in generative AI adoption, with 83% of Chinese respondents using the technology, exceeding both the global average of 54% and the U.S. rate of 65%. This leadership is further evidenced by China's [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property_in_China "Intellectual property in China") developments in the field, with a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN "UN") report revealing that Chinese entities filed over 38,000 generative AI [patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patent "Patent") from 2014 to 2023, substantially surpassing the United States in patent applications.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-62) A 2024 survey on the Chinese social app Soul reported that 18% of respondents born after 2000 used generative AI "almost every day", and that over 60% of respondents like or love AI-generated content, while less than 3% dislike or hate it.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-63)

By mid 2025, despite continued consumer growth, many companies were increasingly abandoning generative AI pilot projects as they had difficulties with integration, data quality and unmet returns, leading analysts to characterize the period as entering the [Gartner hype cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gartner_hype_cycle "Gartner hype cycle")'s "trough of disillusionment" phase.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-65)

Applications
------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Applications")]

Notable types of generative AI models include [generative pre-trained transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer "Generative pre-trained transformer") (GPTs), [generative adversarial networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_adversarial_network "Generative adversarial network") (GANs), and [variational autoencoders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_autoencoder "Variational autoencoder") (VAEs). Generative AI systems are [_multimodal_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodal_learning "Multimodal learning") if they can process multiple types of inputs or generate multiple types of outputs.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-66) For example, [GPT-4o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4o "GPT-4o") can both process and generate text, images and audio.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-67)

Generative AI has made its appearance in a wide variety of industries, radically changing the dynamics of content creation, analysis, and delivery. In healthcare,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-68) for instance, generative AI accelerates [drug discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_discovery "Drug discovery") by creating molecular structures with target characteristics[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-69) and generates [radiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiology "Radiology") images for training diagnostic models. This ability not only enables faster and cheaper development but also enhances medical decision-making. In finance, generative AI services help create datasets and automate reports using natural language. It automates content creation, produces synthetic financial data, and tailors customer communications. It also powers chatbots and virtual agents. Collectively, these technologies enhance efficiency, reduce [operational costs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_costs "Operational costs"), and support data-driven decision-making in financial institutions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-70) The media industry makes use of generative AI for numerous creative activities such as music composition, scriptwriting, video editing, and digital art. The educational sector is impacted as well, since the tools make learning personalized through creating quizzes, study aids, and essay composition. Both the teachers and the learners benefit from AI-based platforms that suit various learning patterns.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-71) In the educational field, in [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia"), student use of [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms")'s generative AI programs resulted in a decline in scores.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-72)

### Text and software code

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Text and software code")]

Main article: [Large language model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model")

See also: [Code completion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_completion "Code completion"), [Autocomplete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocomplete "Autocomplete"), and [Vibe coding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_coding "Vibe coding")

Text generated in 2023 by [Bing Chat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Chat "Bing Chat"), prompted with a question about [Carl Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Jung "Carl Jung")'s concept of [shadow self](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadow_self "Shadow self")[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-73)

Generative AI systems trained on words or [word tokens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_analysis#Tokenization "Lexical analysis") include [GPT-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-3 "GPT-3"), [GPT-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4 "GPT-4"), [GPT-4o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4o "GPT-4o"), [LaMDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaMDA "LaMDA"), [LLaMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLaMA "LLaMA"), [BLOOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BLOOM_(language_model) "BLOOM (language model)"), [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(language_model) "Gemini (language model)"), [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(language_model) "Claude (language model)") and others (see [List of large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_large_language_models "List of large language models")). They are capable of [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing"), [machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation "Machine translation"), and [natural language generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_generation "Natural language generation") and can be used as [foundation models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_models "Foundation models") for other tasks.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-FoundationModels-74) Data sets include [BookCorpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BookCorpus "BookCorpus"), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia"), and others (see [List of text corpora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_text_corpora "List of text corpora")).

In addition to [natural language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language "Natural language") text, large language models can be trained on [programming language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language "Programming language") text, allowing them to generate [source code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_code "Source code") for new [computer programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programs "Computer programs").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-75) Examples include [OpenAI Codex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI_Codex "OpenAI Codex"), [Tabnine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabnine "Tabnine"), [GitHub Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub_Copilot "GitHub Copilot"), [Microsoft Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot "Microsoft Copilot"), and [VS Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VS_Code "VS Code")[fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_(software_development) "Fork (software development)")[Cursor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursor_(code_editor) "Cursor (code editor)").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-76)

Some AI assistants help candidates cheat during online [coding interviews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coding_interview "Coding interview") by providing code, improvements, and explanations. Their clandestine interfaces minimize the need for eye movements that would expose cheating to the interviewer.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:15-77)

### Images

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Images")]

See also: [Text-to-image model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image_model "Text-to-image model") and [Artificial intelligence art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_art "Artificial intelligence art")

Producing high-quality visual art is a prominent application of generative AI.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-78) Generative AI systems trained on sets of images with [text captions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caption_(text) "Caption (text)") include [Imagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagen_(text-to-image_model) "Imagen (text-to-image model)"), [DALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DALL-E "DALL-E"), [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney"), [Adobe Firefly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Firefly "Adobe Firefly"), [FLUX.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FLUX.1 "FLUX.1"), Stable Diffusion and others (see [Artificial intelligence art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_art "Artificial intelligence art"), [Generative art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_art "Generative art"), and [Synthetic media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_media "Synthetic media")). They are commonly used for [text-to-image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image "Text-to-image") generation and [neural style transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_style_transfer "Neural style transfer").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-ZeroShotTextToImage-79) Datasets include [LAION-5B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LAION "LAION") and others (see [List of datasets in computer vision and image processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_datasets_in_computer_vision_and_image_processing "List of datasets in computer vision and image processing")).

### Audio

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Audio")]

See also: [Generative audio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_audio "Generative audio") and [Music and artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_and_artificial_intelligence "Music and artificial intelligence")

Generative AI can also be trained extensively on audio clips to produce natural-sounding [speech synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_synthesis "Speech synthesis") and [text-to-speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-speech "Text-to-speech") capabilities. An early pioneer in this field was [15.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai"), launched in March 2020, which demonstrated the ability to clone character voices using as little as 15 seconds of training data.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-80) The website gained widespread attention for its ability to generate emotionally expressive speech for various fictional characters, though it was later taken offline in 2022 due to copyright concerns.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-83) Commercial alternatives subsequently emerged, including [ElevenLabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ElevenLabs "ElevenLabs")' context-aware synthesis tools and [Meta Platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms")'s Voicebox.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-84)

Music generated in 2022 by the Riffusion Inference Server, prompted with `bossa nova with electric guitar`

Generative AI systems such as [MusicLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicLM "MusicLM")[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-85) and MusicGen[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-86) can also be trained on the audio waveforms of recorded music along with text annotations, in order to generate new musical samples based on text descriptions such as _a calming violin melody backed by a distorted guitar riff_.

[Audio deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_deepfake "Audio deepfake") of music [lyrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyrics "Lyrics") have been generated, like the song Savages, which used AI to mimic rapper [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z")'s vocals. Music artist's instrumentals and lyrics are copyrighted but their voices are not protected from regenerative AI yet, raising a debate about whether artists should get royalties from audio deepfakes.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-87)

### Robotics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Robotics")]

Generative AI can also be trained on the motions of a [robotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotic "Robotic") system to generate new trajectories for [motion planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_planning "Motion planning") or [navigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robot_navigation "Robot navigation"). For example, UniPi from Google Research uses prompts like _"pick up blue bowl"_ or _"wipe plate with yellow sponge"_ to control movements of a robot arm.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-91) Multimodal [vision-language-action models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vision-language-action_model "Vision-language-action model") such as Google's RT-2 can perform rudimentary reasoning in response to user prompts and visual input, such as picking up a toy [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur") when given the prompt _pick up the extinct animal_ at a table filled with toy animals and other objects.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-92)

### 3D modeling

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 3D modeling")]

See also: [Photogrammetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photogrammetry "Photogrammetry")

Artificially intelligent [computer-aided design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-aided_design "Computer-aided design") (CAD) can use text-to-3D, image-to-3D, and video-to-3D to [automate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automate "Automate")[3D modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_modeling "3D modeling").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-93) AI-based [CAD libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_library#CAD_library "Digital library") could also be developed using [linked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linked_data "Linked data")[open data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_data "Open data") of [schematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schematic "Schematic") and [diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagram "Diagram").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-94) AI CAD [assistants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant "Virtual assistant") are used as tools to help streamline workflow.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-95)

Software and hardware
---------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Software and hardware")]

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/GenAI_Agent.png/250px-GenAI_Agent.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GenAI_Agent.png)

Architecture of a generative AI agent

Generative AI models are used to power [chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot") products such as [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"), [programming tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_tools "Programming tools") such as [GitHub Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub_Copilot "GitHub Copilot"),[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-96)[text-to-image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image "Text-to-image") products such as Midjourney, and text-to-video products such as [Runway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runway_(company) "Runway (company)") Gen-2.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-97) Generative AI features have been integrated into a variety of existing commercially available products such as [Microsoft Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Office "Microsoft Office") ([Microsoft Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot "Microsoft Copilot")),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-98)[Google Photos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Photos "Google Photos"),[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-99) and the [Adobe Suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Inc. "Adobe Inc.") ([Adobe Firefly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Firefly "Adobe Firefly")).[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-100) Many generative AI models are also available as [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software"), including Stable Diffusion and the LLaMA[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-101) language model.

Smaller generative AI models with up to a few billion parameters can run on [smartphones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartphones "Smartphones"), embedded devices, and [personal computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computers "Personal computers"). For example, LLaMA-7B (a version with 7 billion parameters) can run on a [Raspberry Pi 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raspberry_Pi_4 "Raspberry Pi 4")[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-102) and one version of Stable Diffusion can run on an [iPhone 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_11 "IPhone 11").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-103)

Larger models with tens of billions of parameters can run on [laptop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laptop "Laptop") or [desktop computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desktop_computers "Desktop computers"). To achieve an acceptable speed, models of this size may require [accelerators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_accelerator "AI accelerator") such as the [GPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPU "GPU") chips produced by [NVIDIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVIDIA "NVIDIA") and [AMD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMD "AMD") or the Neural Engine included in [Apple silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_silicon "Apple silicon") products. For example, the 65 billion parameter version of LLaMA can be configured to run on a desktop PC.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-104)

The advantages of running generative AI locally include protection of [privacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_privacy "Information privacy") and [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property "Intellectual property"), and avoidance of [rate limiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_limiting "Rate limiting") and [censorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship "Censorship"). The [subreddit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reddit "Reddit") r/LocalLLaMA in particular focuses on using [consumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_electronics "Consumer electronics")-grade gaming [graphics cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_card "Graphics card")[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-105) through such techniques as [compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model#Compression "Large language model"). That forum is one of only two sources [Andrej Karpathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrej_Karpathy "Andrej Karpathy") trusts for [language model benchmarks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_model#Evaluation_and_benchmarks "Language model").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-106)[Yann LeCun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_LeCun "Yann LeCun") has advocated open-source models for their value to [vertical applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_market_software "Vertical market software")[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-107) and for improving [AI safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety "AI safety").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-108)

Language models with hundreds of billions of parameters, such as GPT-4 or [PaLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PaLM "PaLM"), typically run on [datacenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datacenter "Datacenter") computers equipped with arrays of [GPUs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPUs "GPUs") (such as NVIDIA's [H100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopper_(microarchitecture) "Hopper (microarchitecture)")) or [AI accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_accelerator "AI accelerator") chips (such as Google's [TPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensor_Processing_Unit "Tensor Processing Unit")). These very large models are typically accessed as [cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") services over the Internet.

In 2022, the [United States New Export Controls on Advanced Computing and Semiconductors to China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_New_Export_Controls_on_Advanced_Computing_and_Semiconductors_to_China "United States New Export Controls on Advanced Computing and Semiconductors to China") imposed restrictions on exports to China of [GPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPU "GPU") and AI accelerator chips used for generative AI.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-109) Chips such as the NVIDIA A800[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-110) and the [Biren Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biren_Technology "Biren Technology") BR104[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-111) were developed to meet the requirements of the sanctions.

There is free software on the market capable of recognizing text generated by generative artificial intelligence (such as [GPTZero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero "GPTZero")), as well as images, audio or video coming from it.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-112) Potential mitigation strategies for [detecting generative AI content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_content_detection "Artificial intelligence content detection") include [digital watermarking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_watermarking "Digital watermarking"), [content authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_provenance "Data provenance"), [information retrieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_retrieval "Information retrieval"), and [machine learning classifier models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning "Supervised learning").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-113) Despite claims of accuracy, both free and paid AI text detectors have frequently produced false positives, mistakenly accusing students of submitting AI-generated work.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-115)

### Generative models and training techniques

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Generative models and training techniques")]

#### Generative adversarial networks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Generative adversarial networks")]

[![Image 10](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/GANs_Technique.webp/250px-GANs_Technique.webp.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GANs_Technique.webp)

Workflow for the training of a generative adversarial network.

[Generative adversarial networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_adversarial_network "Generative adversarial network") (GANs) are an influential generative modeling technique. GANs consist of two neural networks—the generator and the discriminator—trained simultaneously in a competitive setting. The generator creates [synthetic data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_data "Synthetic data") by transforming random noise into samples that resemble the training dataset. The discriminator is trained to distinguish the authentic data from synthetic data produced by the generator.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-116) The two models engage in a [minimax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimax "Minimax") game: the generator aims to create increasingly realistic data to "fool" the discriminator, while the discriminator improves its ability to distinguish real from fake data. This continuous training setup enables the generator to produce high-quality and realistic outputs.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-117)

#### Variational autoencoders

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Variational autoencoders")]

[![Image 11: Two images of the same cartoon crocodile](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/GAN_vs_VAE_%28cropped%29.png/500px-GAN_vs_VAE_%28cropped%29.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GAN_vs_VAE_(cropped).png)

Comparison between images generated by a VAE (left) and a GAN (right). VAEs tend to produce smoother but blurrier images due to their probabilistic decoding.

[Variational autoencoders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_autoencoder "Variational autoencoder") (VAEs) are deep learning models that probabilistically encode data. They are typically used for tasks such as [noise reduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_reduction "Noise reduction") from images, [data compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_compression "Data compression"), identifying unusual patterns, and [facial recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_recognition_system "Facial recognition system"). Unlike [standard autoencoders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoencoder "Autoencoder"), which compress input data into a fixed latent representation, VAEs model the [latent space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latent_space "Latent space") as a probability distribution,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-118) allowing for smooth sampling and interpolation between data points. The encoder ("recognition model") maps input data to a latent space, producing means and variances that define a probability distribution. The decoder ("generative model") samples from this latent distribution and attempts to reconstruct the original input. VAEs optimize a loss function that includes both the reconstruction error and a [Kullback–Leibler divergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kullback%E2%80%93Leibler_divergence "Kullback–Leibler divergence") term, which ensures the latent space follows a known prior distribution. VAEs are particularly suitable for tasks that require structured but smooth latent spaces, although they may create blurrier images than GANs. They are used for applications like image generation, data interpolation and [anomaly detection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomaly_detection "Anomaly detection").

[![Image 12: The full architecture of a GPT model.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Full_GPT_architecture.png/330px-Full_GPT_architecture.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Full_GPT_architecture.png)

The full architecture of a GPT model.

##### Transformers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Transformers")]

Transformers became the foundation for many powerful generative models, most notably the [generative pre-trained transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer "Generative pre-trained transformer") (GPT) series developed by OpenAI. They marked a major shift in natural language processing by replacing traditional [recurrent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recurrent_neural_network "Recurrent neural network") and [convolutional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolutional_neural_network "Convolutional neural network") models.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-119) This architecture allows models to process entire sequences simultaneously and capture long-range dependencies more efficiently. The [self-attention mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_(machine_learning) "Attention (machine learning)") enables the model to capture the significance of every word in a sequence when predicting the subsequent word, thus improving its contextual understanding. Unlike recurrent neural networks, transformers process all the tokens in parallel, which improves the training efficiency and scalability. Transformers are typically pre-trained on enormous corpora in a [self-supervised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-supervised_learning "Self-supervised learning") manner, prior to being [fine-tuned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine-tuning_(deep_learning) "Fine-tuning (deep learning)").

Law and regulation
------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Law and regulation")]

Main article: [Regulation of artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_artificial_intelligence "Regulation of artificial intelligence")

In the United States, a group of companies including OpenAI, Alphabet, and Meta signed a voluntary agreement with the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration") in July 2023 to watermark AI-generated content.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-120) In October 2023, [Executive Order 14110](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order_14110 "Executive Order 14110") applied the [Defense Production Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Production_Act "Defense Production Act") to require all US companies to report information to the federal government when training certain high-impact AI models.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-122)

In the European Union, the proposed [Artificial Intelligence Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence_Act "Artificial Intelligence Act") includes requirements to disclose copyrighted material used to train generative AI systems, and to label any AI-generated output as such.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-124)

In China, the [Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interim_Measures_for_the_Management_of_Generative_AI_Services "Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services") introduced by the [Cyberspace Administration of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberspace_Administration_of_China "Cyberspace Administration of China") regulates any public-facing generative AI. It includes requirements to watermark generated images or videos, regulations on training data and label quality, restrictions on personal data collection, and a guideline that generative AI services must "adhere to socialist core values".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-125)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-126)

### Copyright

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Copyright")]

Main article: [Artificial intelligence and copyright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_and_copyright "Artificial intelligence and copyright")

#### Training with copyrighted content

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Training with copyrighted content")]

Generative AI systems such as [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT") and [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney") are trained on large, publicly available datasets that include copyrighted works. AI developers have argued that such training is protected under [fair use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_use "Fair use"), while copyright holders have argued that it infringes their rights.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-crscopyright-127)

Proponents of fair use training have argued that it is a [transformative use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformative_use "Transformative use") and does not involve making copies of copyrighted works available to the public.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-crscopyright-127) Critics have argued that image generators such as [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney") can create nearly-identical copies of some copyrighted images,[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-128) and that generative AI programs compete with the content they are trained on.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-129)

As of 2024, several lawsuits related to the use of copyrighted material in training are ongoing. [Getty Images](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getty_Images "Getty Images") has sued [Stability AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stability_AI "Stability AI") over the use of its images to train [Stable Diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion "Stable Diffusion").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-130) Both the [Authors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authors_Guild "Authors Guild") and [The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times") have sued [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") and [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI") over the use of their works to train [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-132)

#### Copyright of AI-generated content

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Copyright of AI-generated content")]

A separate question is whether AI-generated works can qualify for copyright protection. The [United States Copyright Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Copyright_Office "United States Copyright Office") has ruled that works created by artificial intelligence without any human input cannot be copyrighted, because they lack human authorship.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-133) Some legal professionals have suggested that _[Naruto v. Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey\_selfie\_copyright\_dispute "Monkey selfie copyright dispute")_ (2018), in which the [U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._9th_Circuit_Court_of_Appeals "U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals") held that [non-humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-human "Non-human") cannot be copyright holders of [artistic works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal-made_art "Animal-made art"), could be a potential precedent in copyright litigation over works created by generative AI.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-134) However, the office has also begun taking public input to determine if these rules need to be refined for generative AI.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-135)

In January 2025, the [United States Copyright Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Copyright_Office "United States Copyright Office") (USCO) released extensive guidance regarding the use of AI tools in the creative process, and established that "...generative AI systems also offer tools that similarly allow users to exert control. [These] can enable the user to control the selection and placement of individual creative elements. Whether such modifications rise to the minimum standard of originality required under [Feist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feist_Publications,_Inc.,_v._Rural_Telephone_Service_Co. "Feist Publications, Inc., v. Rural Telephone Service Co.") will depend on a case-by-case determination. In those cases where they do, the output should be copyrightable"[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-136) Subsequently, the USCO registered the first visual artwork to be composed of entirely AI-generated materials, titled "A Single Piece of American Cheese".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-137)

Concerns
--------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Concerns")]

See also: [Ethics of artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics_of_artificial_intelligence "Ethics of artificial intelligence")

The development of generative AI has raised concerns from [governments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government "Government"), businesses, and individuals, resulting in protests, legal actions, calls to [pause AI experiments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pause_Giant_AI_Experiments:_An_Open_Letter "Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter"), and actions by multiple governments. In a July 2023 briefing of the [United Nations Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"), [Secretary-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations")[António Guterres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres "António Guterres") stated "Generative AI has enormous potential for good and evil at scale", that AI may "turbocharge global development" and contribute between $10 and $15 trillion to the global economy by 2030, but that its malicious use "could cause horrific levels of death and destruction, widespread trauma, and deep psychological damage on an unimaginable scale".[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-138) In addition, generative AI has a significant [carbon footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_footprint "Carbon footprint").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:82-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:14-140)

### Academic honesty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Academic honesty")]

Generative AI can be used to generate and modify academic prose, to paraphrasing sources, and translate languages. The use of generative AI in a classroom setting can be a form of [academic plagiarism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_dishonesty#Plagiarism "Academic dishonesty"). Some schools have banned ChatGPT and similar tools.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Barrett-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Chan2023-142)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS "Wikipedia:NOTRS")_]

A commonly proposed use for teachers is grading and giving feedback. Companies like Pearson and ETS use AI to score grammar, mechanics, usage, and style, but not for main ideas or overall structure.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Barrett-141) The National Council of Teachers of English says machine scoring makes students feel their writing isn't worth reading.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-143) AI scoring has also given unfair results for students from different ethnic backgrounds.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-144)

### Job losses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Job losses")]

Main articles: [Workplace impact of artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workplace_impact_of_artificial_intelligence "Workplace impact of artificial intelligence") and [Technological unemployment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_unemployment "Technological unemployment")

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/AI_Protest_Sign_2023_WGA_Strike.jpg/250px-AI_Protest_Sign_2023_WGA_Strike.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AI_Protest_Sign_2023_WGA_Strike.jpg)

A picketer at the [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). While not a top priority, one of the WGA's 2023 requests was "regulations around the use of (generative) AI".[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-145)

From the early days of the development of AI, there have been arguments put forward by [ELIZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA "ELIZA") creator [Joseph Weizenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Weizenbaum "Joseph Weizenbaum") and others about whether tasks that can be done by computers actually should be done by them, given the difference between computers and humans, and between quantitative calculations and qualitative, value-based judgements.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-146) In April 2023, it was reported that image generation AI has resulted in 70% of the jobs for video game illustrators in China being lost.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-148) In July 2023, developments in generative AI contributed to the [2023 Hollywood labor disputes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hollywood_labor_disputes "2023 Hollywood labor disputes"). [Fran Drescher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_Drescher "Fran Drescher"), president of the [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild"), declared that "artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to creative professions" during the [2023 SAG-AFTRA strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SAG-AFTRA_strike "2023 SAG-AFTRA strike").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-149) Voice generation AI has been seen as a potential challenge to the [voice acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_acting "Voice acting") sector.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-151)

The intersection of AI and employment concerns among underrepresented groups globally remains a critical facet. While AI promises efficiency enhancements and skill acquisition, concerns about job displacement and biased recruiting processes persist among these groups, as outlined in surveys by [Fast Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Company "Fast Company"). To leverage AI for a more equitable society, proactive steps encompass mitigating biases, advocating transparency, respecting privacy and consent, and embracing diverse teams and ethical considerations. Strategies involve redirecting policy emphasis on regulation, inclusive design, and education's potential for personalized teaching to maximize benefits while minimizing harms.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-152)

### Racial and gender bias

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Racial and gender bias")]

Generative AI models can reflect and amplify any [cultural bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_bias "Cultural bias") present in the underlying data. For example, a language model might assume that doctors and judges are male, and that secretaries or nurses are female, if those biases are common in the training data.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-153) Similarly, an image model prompted with the text "a photo of a CEO" might disproportionately generate images of white male CEOs,[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-154) if trained on a racially biased data set. A number of methods for mitigating bias have been attempted, such as altering input prompts[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-155) and reweighting training data.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-DALL-E2-mitigations-156)

### Deepfakes

network").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:3-158) Deepfakes have garnered widespread attention and concerns for their uses in [deepfake celebrity pornographic videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfake_pornography "Deepfake pornography"), [revenge porn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenge_porn "Revenge porn"), [fake
